Chapter 1 · Executive summary

What the pilot needs to prove

Everything in this proposal serves one decision: connect one real production and test whether Tubes gives MMG earlier, more reliable financial visibility without taking operational control away from the production company. Four questions decide it.

Earlier
Forecast movement before the reporting cycle

Do you see commitments and ETC move the EFC before the normal report would show it?

Comparable
One financial structure across companies

Can different production companies report through the same structure?

Less manual
Consolidation without assembly

Does MMG spend less time collecting and consolidating reports?

Non-intrusive
Visibility without takeover

Does the production company keep running its production, workflows intact?

The chapters that follow explain how Tubes intends to prove those four things with one real production.

Chapter 2 · Two versions of Tubes

One follows. The other runs.

Tubes is production software with management overviews on top, for one or more underlying production companies. The companies work in it; Motion Media Group watches over it. That distinction matters, because it means MMG never has to operate inside a production's books to see what is happening in them. Tubes Portfolio is a control layer built on the live production data underneath, not another dashboard fed by reports.

For Motion Media Group

MMG Tubes Portfolio

  • One live view over every connected production, built on the data underneath
  • Early warnings the day a forecast moves past budget
  • Cashflow and margin forecast per company, month, quarter, year
  • Price per minute and per episode, comparable across the slate
  • Drill-down: portfolio → company → production → invoice
  • Read-only share links for investor reporting
  • Standard setup and templates, rolled out group-wide
Follow and steer, without running the productions.
For every company or film you finance

Tubes Production

  • One or more productions and series per workspace
  • Create projects; build budgets or import Movie Magic directly
  • Real-time cost control: budget → PO → invoice → forecast
  • Invoice processing with automatic reading and approvals
  • Xero or other accounting software, connected when wanted
  • Day planning, call sheets and a crew app on the same data
  • Local currency and language per company; fixed exchange rates per production
Run the production, head office sees the rollup.

Chapter 3 · Getting connected

How a production company joins

The connection is a weblink. Workspace setup takes minutes; operational adoption is gradual, along the phased path in chapter 12.

1

MMG sends its signup link

The link carries your group profile: cost structure, roles, approval rules and, optionally, your standard budget and format templates.

2

The company creates its own workspace

Five to ten minutes of self-onboarding. The workspace arrives pre-configured, so every company across the group starts from the same structure and reports the same way.

3

The connection is live

From the first project the team creates, its numbers roll up into MMG's portfolio dashboard, automatically, in real time.

4

Support when needed, where needed

We support companies during signup, give training where that helps, and stay involved until a team runs on its own. Most teams need little of it; the point is that the help is there.

Chapter 4 · Budgets & Movie Magic

Build the budget, or import it

A team can build its budget in Tubes: budget lines organised by cost group, versions to compare scenarios, a locked version as the approved baseline, and a work budget for the team's day-to-day view. Or, and this is the path we expect most of your teams to take, it uploads its existing Movie Magic budget, which becomes the live baseline in minutes. Nobody rebuilds anything.

Movie Magic is still widely used for building budgets, and teams that like it can keep it. The difference is everything that happens after the budget. Keep the tools that work; connect the information that matters.

Chapter 5 · Cost control in real time

Six numbers, from first budget to final cost

How it works: every purchase order and every invoice is entered against a budget line, that single discipline is what makes everything else automatic. The moment a PO is raised, the committed total and the estimated final cost move. The team sees its own variance live; nobody waits for a cost report to find out where they stand.

Baseline
Budget
Working
Work budget
Committed
Planned / PO

Cost to date
Ledger
Transactions
Outlook
EFC & variance

The model is always the same: approved budget → work budget → committed (PO) → actuals (CTD) + ETC → EFC, with variance and the cash requirement following from it. Transactions are not a stage after CTD; they are the input that becomes CTD. The forecast stays anchored to actual costs and commitments, while ETC captures what the team still expects to spend.

Chapter 6 · Invoices & accounting

From inbox to books, without re-keying

How it works: an invoice is dropped in (or mailed in), and Tubes reads it, supplier, amounts, dates, and proposes the budget line it belongs to. A person confirms; approval rules route it to whoever has to sign off at that amount. Once approved, it counts in cost to date and the forecast, immediately.

If the company uses Xero or other accounting software, the connection keeps the production ledger and the books aligned, no double entry, no month-end surprise where the two disagree. Teams that prefer exports get exports.

Chapter 8 · AI in Tubes

The assistant behind the production

AI in Tubes is there to remove the reading, checking and drafting that consumes production-finance time, not to make decisions on people’s behalf. Every AI-generated suggestion is clearly identified, and every decision remains with a person. In Tubes, violet marks the assistant, so you always know what came from AI.

Draft budgets

Describe the production, format and target amount, and the assistant creates a first budget for the team to refine. It gets a production to a workable starting point faster, particularly for recurring formats. The assistant drafts; the team decides.

Read invoices and documents

Invoices are read automatically and key information is extracted: supplier, amounts, dates and a proposed budget line. A person confirms the result, and approvals remain human.

Watch the numbers

As a production runs, the assistant monitors costs against budget and flags what deserves attention: by team or department on the production, and rolled up across the group for MMG.

Learn from the finish

When a production wraps, the assistant compares budget to final cost by cost type and highlights what the next production could do differently.

Translate automatically

Language does not have to be a barrier. The assistant translates between Tubes’ ten supported languages, so an international production team and head office can work from the same information in their own language.

Every suggestion is visible, attributable and reversible. AI usage is managed through monthly credits per workspace, keeping the cost predictable.

Where it’s heading

The ambition is simple: empower productions to spend more time making things and less time reconciling spreadsheets, while giving the people financing them a live view of where things stand.

AI takes that further. The direction is towards operating Tubes through conversation: ask a question and get a live answer; give an instruction and have the assistant prepare the work for a person to review and approve. The system does the work around the decision. The person stays in control.

Tubes Assistant
How is The Long Season doing against budget?
It's $14k under, the tightest margin on the slate. EFC is $11.99M against a $12.0M budget, with cost type 2000 CREW closest to its line. Want the breakdown per line?
Yes, and prepare a note for Thursday's production meeting.
Breakdown is open on your screen. The note is drafted and waiting for your approval before it goes to the team.

Chapter 9 · Planning, call sheets & crew

One plan, one source of truth

Production teams plan their days in Tubes, build call sheets directly from that planning, and publish them when they’re ready. Schedules and published call sheets then land straight on the crew’s phones through the Tubes mobile app: no PDF chains, no version confusion, no wondering which document is current.

And because the production plan sits alongside the budget, the operational and financial pictures stay connected. The people planning the work and the people tracking the money are working from the same underlying data, rather than maintaining two separate versions of the production.

Chapter 10 · Currencies & languages

Built for a slate that crosses borders

Your productions already span jurisdictions, from Canada and Puerto Rico to India and Africa. Tubes is built for that reality from the start, with local currencies, local workflows and multilingual access, while giving the group a consistent view across the slate.

Currency
Local currency, fixed FX

Each production company works in the currency it actually uses. Budgets, purchase orders and invoices stay in local currency, with a fixed exchange rate set for each production. The group can then report in a common currency without teams having to convert anything manually or worry about exchange-rate movements distorting the production budget.

Language
10 languages

Tubes supports 10 languages, set at workspace or individual-user level. A Dutch line producer and a Canadian accountant can work on the same production, each in their own language. Additional languages can be added as needed.

Getting started
Live in minutes, not weeks

A workspace can be set up quickly using standard templates and configuration. There is no need for a lengthy implementation project before a team can start working.

How it works across borders. The production company works entirely in its own local currency. Tubes handles the fixed exchange rate at production level, allowing the group rollup to report consistently without changing the underlying numbers.

Chapter 11 · Data separation & permissions

Who sees what, by design

Every production company works in its own, separate workspace. Its data belongs to that company, with its own permissions and controls. MMG’s portfolio workspace provides the group-level view, with the ability to drill into the productions it finances, without operating inside the company’s books. Companies remain fully separated from one another.

Within each workspace, role-based permissions determine exactly who can see and do what. A line producer sees the productions they work on. A department head can be limited to their own work budget. An accountant can have access to the financial information they need without necessarily seeing rates. Approval rules can put a named person between a significant commitment and the money.

This same separation works at group level. MMG gets the transparency it needs across the productions it finances, while each company keeps control of its own data and operations. Portfolio access is read-only: MMG can see and drill into the data, but cannot edit it.

Chapter 12 · Adoption path & pilot

Gradual by design, starting with a pilot

Tubes doesn’t ask a team to change the way it works all at once. Start with the data you already have, get visibility from day one, then bring more of the workflow into the system when the team is ready. Each team can move at its own pace, while the value builds from the start.

1

Import and see

Workspaces created via your signup link. Current Movie Magic budgets imported. Costs start landing against budget lines. Your portfolio view is live.

First

Then
3

Run

Day planning, call sheets and the crew app, production operations on the same data as the money.

When a team wants it

The pilot

The quickest way to judge this is to look at one of your own productions through it.

  • Pick one production you finance. Its team signs up through your link and imports its current budget.
  • Set up the MMG portfolio workspace, configured with your standard setup and templates, ready to roll out further later.
  • Follow the production live: budget, commitments, cost to date and forecast, from the portfolio dashboard down to the invoice.
  • Then decide. If the picture isn't sharper than what you have today, that is the end of it.
Plan the walkthrough or write me directly, joachim@tubes.media
